name: Central Plains Industries LLC
old_description: This video is one of our high performance, expert arc welding industrial robots. These save on costs while increasing accuracy.
about:
Central Plains Industries LLC operates a metal fabrication shop in Clark, South Dakota, roughly 20 miles west of Watertown. The company was founded in 2001. No founders or ownership details are disclosed.

The facility spans over 120,000 square feet and houses a full range of metalworking capabilities under one roof. Cutting services include laser, plasma, and band saw cutting. Fabrication equipment covers press brakes, benders, a corner notcher, powered shear, sheet metal roller, turret punches, and a powered sheet metal punch with a large tooling selection. Machining centers feature twin-spindle, twin-turret configurations with live milling and robotic part unloading, controlled by Siemens CNC systems. Welding capabilities encompass line, spot, robotic, TIG, and MIG processes. Finishing options include liquid painting, undercoating, and powder coating for industrial and automotive applications. The company employs a dedicated workforce, though exact headcount is not public.

Central Plains serves industrial and automotive sectors, along with other markets requiring custom metal fabrication, machining, and finishing. Customers include repeat buyers who value on-time delivery and competitive pricing, as reflected in testimonials from individuals such as Dave Oster, Troy Reil, and a reviewer on MFG.com.

The company states its mission is to be the custom fabricator for its markets by creating value and relationships where all succeed. It emphasizes continuous improvement, quality checks at every operation step using Faro Arm, scanner, and digital gauges, and a commitment to delivering parts to the customer's dock on schedule.

name: Central Sheet Metal Products Inc
old_description: Central Sheet Metal Products is a family owned and operated precision sheet metal fabricator since 1912.
about:
Central Sheet Metal Products, Inc. has operated from Skokie, Illinois since 1912. The company was founded as a Chicago storefront supplying copper, roof flashings, gutters and downspouts, and has remained in the Silverstein family for five generations. Current leadership includes fourth‑generation owners Joel and Peter Silverstein and fifth‑generation owners Ron and Rob Silverstein.

The shop specializes in precision sheet metal fabrication, offering fiber laser cutting with lights‑out automation, CNC punching and forming, welding, drilling/tapping, hardware insertion, polishing and contract finishing (powder coating, e‑coating, painting, silk screening, plating and anodizing). Engineering is performed in‑house using SolidWorks 3D modeling, with design, reverse‑engineering and re‑engineering services. The facility runs multiple press brakes (up to 135 metric tons), a Mitsubishi 2.5 kW fiber laser with a 120″ × 60″ bed, Strippit turret punches, and a range of secondary equipment. The company handles small, medium and large volume runs and multiple part‑mix OEM programs.

Customers span OEM medical and dental devices, electronics, rack‑mount and audio/visual enclosures, computer peripherals, industrial equipment, electrical and air‑handling systems, display/POP, gaming, food‑and‑beverage vending, and agricultural machinery. The firm focuses on contract manufacturing for original equipment manufacturers.

The company emphasizes quality craftsmanship, complete customer satisfaction, direct communication, on‑time delivery and continuous improvement. Capital investments in automation and calibration have reduced lead times, and a business‑continuity mindset aims to maintain consistent service across generations.

name: Cerac, Inc.
old_description: As the world's leading manufacturer of engineered, specialty strip metal solutions and copper-beryllium rod and wire products, we offer the widest range of reel-to-reel and screw machinable materials for a variety of high-performance connectors for 5G and big data applications.
about:
Cerac, Inc. is headquartered in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. The company traces its origins to 1921, when it began unlocking the potential of beryllium for advanced industrial applications. Over nearly a century, it has grown into a global advanced materials enterprise.

The company manufactures specialty engineered alloy systems, inorganic chemicals and powders, precious and non-precious metals, beryllium and beryllium composites, and precision filters and optical coatings. Its core product lines include engineered strip metal solutions and copper-beryllium rod and wire, produced via reel-to-reel and screw-machinable processes. Operations span more than 30 locations worldwide with a workforce exceeding 3,000 employees.

Cerac serves customers in semiconductor, industrial, aerospace and defense, energy, automotive, telecommunications and data center, and consumer electronics markets. Its materials enable high-performance connectors for 5G and big data infrastructure, thermal management for rocket engines, and nuclear-grade beryllium for clean energy projects.

The company states its purpose is to push the boundaries of innovation to enable breakthrough solutions that move the world forward. It differentiates itself through the widest range of reel-to-reel and screw-machinable copper-beryllium products, integrated analysis, testing, engineering, and recycling services, and a legacy of nearly 100 years in beryllium and advanced materials expertise.

about:
Challenge Electronics, Inc. was established in 1991 in East Providence, Rhode Island. The company operates as a full-service electronics center from its location serving both business and personal electronics needs.

The firm specializes in two-way communications, marine electronics systems, GPS navigation, and satellite communications. Its team of sales and technical service specialists provides product selection, installation, and ongoing support for land mobile radio and marine equipment. The company also operates a sister firm focused on marine electronics.

Challenge Electronics serves customers in the two-way radio, marine electronics, and specialty electronics sectors. Its client base includes commercial fleets, public safety agencies, and recreational boaters seeking communication and navigation solutions. The company represents brands such as Motorola, as indicated by its authorized use of Motorola trademarks.

The company emphasizes total customer satisfaction and positions itself as a resource for land mobile communications and marine systems, drawing on over three decades of experience since its founding.

name: Champion Petfoods USA
old_description: Founded in a small town in Alberta, Canada, Champion has grown to be a key player in the premium pet food industry with products sold in over 90 countries. By focusing exclusively on crafting premium pet food, we perfect our recipes and innovate new, quality foods that help pets thrive for a lifetime.
about:
Champion Petfoods USA, headquartered in Auburn, Kentucky, traces its origins to 1985 when the company was founded in a small town in Alberta, Canada. The business began with a singular focus on crafting premium pet food and has since expanded to serve pet owners in more than 90 countries worldwide.

The company manufactures two primary brands, ORIJEN and ACANA, for dogs and cats. Its process centers on sourcing WholePrey animal ingredients — meat, poultry, and fish — from a curated supplier network, which are then formulated by Ph.D.-level nutrition experts and veterinarians and produced in what the company describes as state-of-the-art kitchens. ORIJEN recipes contain up to 90 percent animal ingredients, while ACANA balances protein-rich animal ingredients with whole fruits and vegetables.

Champion serves the premium pet food industry globally, with a presence across three major geographic regions. Its customer base includes independent and neighborhood pet retailers, supported through a founding sponsorship of IndiePet, as well as direct consumer sales. The company also collaborates with the University of Guelph on pet nutrition science.

The company states that its exclusive focus on premium pet food allows it to perfect recipes and innovate new products, emphasizing that it never adds wheat, corn, or soy in its kitchens. Its stated mission is to provide peak nutrition, optimal nourishment, and ultimate flavor so pet lovers can feel confident feeding their dogs and cats.

about:
Champion Plastics, based in Clifton, New Jersey, has been producing polyethylene packaging since 1972. The company operates an 18-acre manufacturing campus that includes one of the industry's largest resin storage silos, with a capacity of 2,000 tons.

The company manufactures a broad line of polyethylene bags, liners, covers, films, sheeting, tubing, and shrink packaging. Its capabilities include custom sizes, gauges, and configurations, with gauge ranges from 0.0005 to 0.010 mil, and options for additives such as EVA, UV inhibitors, anti-static, and flame retardant. The facility supports printing up to 10 colors and various packaging formats.

Champion Plastics serves a wide range of industries, including pharmaceutical, food processing, chemical, industrial manufacturing, medical waste, and retail. Its customer base includes Fortune 500 companies across sectors such as aerospace, automotive, agriculture, construction, and textiles.

The company emphasizes its broad product selection, competitive pricing, responsive service, and dependable delivery as key differentiators. It maintains ISO 9001:2015 certification to ensure consistent quality and traceability.

name: Champion Steel Works
old_description: Managing construction projects can be stressful. At Champion Steel Works, we deliver stress-free steel you can trust -- giving contractors the confidence and credibility to succeed.
about:
Champion Steel Works, operating in Wilmington, Ohio, traces its roots to 1872 when it began as Champion Bridge Company. The family-led business has been passed down through generations; current president Noah Dell succeeded his father, continuing a legacy of serving the community with integrity and gratitude.

The company fabricates structural steel, producing more than 60 tons per week at its Wilmington shop. Its services span steel fabrication, project management, job order contract (JOC) proposal support, and local metal supply. The process emphasizes early plan analysis, conflict identification, fabrication to specification, quality inspection, and scheduled delivery to match project timelines.

Champion serves contractors across Ohio, Kentucky, the Carolinas, Indiana, Tennessee, Michigan, Georgia, Alabama, and Florida, with projects including healthcare facilities such as Winton Hills Medical Center and a new medical office building. The firm also supplies metal to residents and businesses throughout Clinton County.

about:
Charlotte Wire & Cable Company Inc. was founded in 1993 in Concord, North Carolina, by Mike Biggers, who serves as president and founder. The company began as a wire and cable distributor committed to selling exclusively through the electrical distribution channel.

The company stocks over 2,000 wire and cable products, including building wire, utility wire, and specialized cables, across a combined 150,000 square feet of warehouse and office space. It operates as a distributor, providing 24/7 emergency service and dedicated customer support.

Charlotte Wire & Cable serves industrial and manufacturing, residential and commercial, utility and infrastructure, and logistics and transportation sectors. Its customer base consists of electrical distributors who rely on the company’s industry-specific knowledge and prompt delivery across all 50 states.

Founder Mike Biggers emphasizes the company’s “through the electrical distribution channel” sales policy as a core differentiator, aiming to provide courteous, prompt service, high-quality products, and reliable on-time delivery to distributor partners.

name: Charter Medical LLC
old_description: We deliver scalable, single-use solutions designed for your advanced processes. Built to help you make the impossible, possible.
about:
Charter Medical LLC operates from Winston-Salem, North Carolina. The company has nearly 35 years of experience developing single-use products for life sciences, though a founding year is not disclosed. It operates as part of the Solesis family of companies alongside sister firms Polyzen, Secant Group, and SanaVita Medical.

The company designs and manufactures scalable single-use solutions including bio-containers, fluid transfer sets, bags, filters, and manifolds for bioprocessing, blood management, cell and gene therapy, and cryopreservation. Its 16,000-square-foot cleanroom facility in Winston-Salem is ISO 13485-certified and FDA-registered, supporting custom product design and manufacturing from prototype to commercial scale.

Charter Medical serves the cell therapy, blood transfusion, biotechnology, and pharmaceutical markets. Its customers include biopharmaceutical innovators developing advanced therapies who require customizable single-use systems for upstream and downstream processing, fluid transfer, filtration, and cold-chain storage.

The company emphasizes proven customization capabilities, an innovation roadmap in design and biomaterials, and a commitment to responsiveness and collaboration to reduce cost and risk in delivering advanced therapies. Integrated R&D with Solesis sister companies further supports technology development.

name: Cherry Brook Woodworks
old_description: Cherry Brook Woodworks creates custom designed furniture, historic reproductions, their own designs, and also repairs valuable antiques.  Working for individual homeowners, architects, interior designers, and museums, Cherry Brook Woodworks builds custom furniture that will fit in any environment and will last for generations.
about:
Cherry Brook Woodworks operates from Canton, Connecticut, where in 2001 the Aleksa family purchased a home in the historic district and converted two antique apple barns into a woodworking shop. The business was founded by Peter Aleksa, a fine furniture maker who had spent years training under a master German craftsman and working in Connecticut shops specializing in period furniture and restoration.

The shop produces custom furniture, museum-quality antique reproductions, and repair and restoration services for heirloom pieces, all made by hand using traditional joinery and period-appropriate finishes. The workspace remains in the original barn structures on the family property, and the output ranges from one-off commissions to a rotating catalog of original designs such as Shaker tripod tables, sideboards, and chests crafted in tiger maple, birdseye maple, cherry, white oak, and walnut.

Clients include individual homeowners, interior designers, architects, and museums, with pieces shipped throughout the United States. The company has reproduced historic furniture from photographs or originals for institutional clients and restored family heirlooms for private owners.

Aleksa emphasizes a collaborative process, listening closely to each client to create furniture that fits specific spaces and styles, a level of personal involvement he contrasts with larger production shops. His approach stems from a belief that the relationship with the client is as important as the finished piece, and that honoring the materials and history behind each project results in furniture built to last generations.
